decision: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING — Frozen decision_rule requires ALL C1-C5 for SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. C5 (NULL-NO-SHARING) fails under correct computation: isolated null-control ratio for 3 search tasks is 1.253 (param 104 tokens / literal 83 tokens), not ~1.0 as required by spec expected_behavior; code hardcodes c5_pass=True via self-ratio (search_param/search_param). Additionally C1 violates measurement_validity[0]: spec requires mechanisms from existing SPIDER registry/task corpus, but producer uses hardcoded synthetic TASK_CORPUS (32 tasks in run_experiment.py), violating the frozen population contract. Per frozen ALL-must-pass rule, FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING triggers. However, the arithmetic is verified: on the as-implemented synthetic 32-task corpus, parameterized representation yields 25 vs 32 mechanisms (21.9% reduction) and 679 vs 791 tokens (0.8584 dedup ratio, 112 tokens/14.16% savings) because 3 of 25 patterns are shared across 2-5 tasks. The savings are a lower bound (heuristic missed admin u-aaa class, true dedup ratio ~0.757 and savings ~24.3% if corrected). Per-task analysis reveals shared patterns incur -15.8% per-task penalty (parameterized costs MORE per task) but corpus savings arise from storing the pattern once instead of N times. The null-control failure is informative: unique patterns show 25.3% overhead from ${slot} syntax, meaning deduplication wins only when sharing frequency exceeds the per-pattern overhead threshold. No product promotion. C-PRODUCT-ECON remains HYPOTHESIS (frozen gate failed, measurement validity violated). C-PARAM-INHERIT remains EXPERIMENTAL.
